correctness.rationale: PASS: Iterating a partial function produces a terminal path or a unique lasso. The formulas Θ_h, loop(a^d) excluding loops at proper divisors, and Λ_(t,d) with the negative predecessor loop(a⁺) test isolate all labels t+d≤n. Isomorphism of the root-generated forward substructure preserves all permitted program interpretations including tests and loops by induction. Without loop every serial one-action component is bisimilar, while Θ_h separates terminating distances. Finite disjunctions realize every subset. Independently enumerated (n+1)^n labelled partial functions and all roots for n≤5 (38,880 at n=5) matching L_n.

value.rationale: PASS: The complete model-theoretic quotient and sharp exponential semantic-algebra gap quantify exactly what the loop operator adds in a natural deterministic, atom-free test class. This is a useful finite baseline for return-sensitive program logic; it is not presented as a general finite-satisfiability solution.

final_claim: On finite pointed partial-functional single-action models with no propositional atoms, converse or global actions, roots are variable-free LoopPDL-equivalent iff they have the same terminating distance h or lasso preperiod t and period d. Among frames of at most n worlds the quotient has n(n+3)/2 types and 2^[n(n+3)/2] formula meanings; ordinary PDL without loop has n+1 types and 2^(n+1) meanings.
limitations: Counting pertains to formula equivalence over models with at most n worlds, not formula length/minimum size or arbitrary frames.
Finite enumeration through n=5 is corroboration only; all-n proof uses structural induction.
